advances: Exact planar directional calculation at specified triangle tent data for the symmetric profile bodies.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Slicing the triangle by a fixed axial coordinate gives two linear section lengths, meeting at the middle vertex height. Degenerate rising or falling intervals give facet endpoints. The area fixes the tent height $2/w$. Its axial mean is the average of the three axial vertex heights, which gives $a,b,c$ as stated. Integrating gives the continuous tail $F(s)$ equal to $1$ for $s\le a$, $1-(s-a)^2/(\theta w^2)$ for $a\le s\le b$, $(c-s)^2/((1-\theta)w^2)$ for $b\le s\le c$, and $0$ for $s\ge c$, omitting a zero-length proper interval. The kite realizes exactly this profile and has centroid zero. Minkowski averaging of two convex hulls gives the hull of all vertex midpoints. The quadratic cells of the paired sum are separated by $a_A,b_A,c_A,-a_B,-b_B,-c_B$, and the far plateau is one. Thus the finite tests give the minimum. Rationality of the polygon area and halfplane area follows by rational segment clipping and the polygon area formula.

At a fixed axial level, the longest centered interval is found by allocating the available displacement to the largest slopes first. Each segment of an individual tent has a slope no greater than its predecessors, so this order respects the available prefixes. Exchanging displacement from a smaller selected slope to a larger unfilled one only increases the height. In the midpoint roof the rising components have lengths $p/2,Rq/2$ and respective gains $1,1/R$, and the falling components have lengths $a'/2,Rb'/2$ and respective losses $1,1/R$. This yields rise order $A,B$ if $p\le R^2q$ and $B,A$ otherwise, and fall order $B,A$ if $a'\le R^2b'$ and $A,B$ otherwise. Both exceptions cannot hold since their sum would give $1>R^2$. Summing the corresponding trapezoids gives the three values of $m$.

The first segment ends at $(2p-1-R(1+q))/6\le0$ in the $A$-first case, and at $(2Rq-R-1-p)/6\le(2p/R-R-1-p)/6\le0$ in the $B$-first case. Reflection gives that the last segment starts at or above zero. The peak is at $H$, and the right support is $S/2$. Thus for $H\le0$ the zero cut lies on the first fall, including its boundaries. If the last fall belongs to $A$, its triangle has length $a'/2$, height one and area $a'/4$, while the first fall from zero to the start of the last has length $(S-a')/2$ and slope $-2/(R^2b')$. Summing the two areas gives the first displayed formula. For a last $B$ fall replace its length and height by $Rb'/2$ and $1/R$ and use first-fall slope $-2/a'$, giving the second formula. Reflection gives the other sign of $H$. Zero-length components can be omitted by the polygon construction or by Hausdorff continuity of convex hulls and convergence of their cap areas, since the limiting polygon boundary and cutting line have area zero.
statement:
The axial length profile of a centered area-one triangle is a tent of width $w>0$, mode fraction $\theta\in[0,1]$, peak height $2/w$ and support/mode coordinates
$$
a=-(1+\theta)w/3,\qquad b=(2\theta-1)w/3,\qquad c=(2-\theta)w/3.
$$
The kite $E_{w,\theta}=\operatorname{conv}\{(a,0),(b,1/w),(c,0),(b,-1/w)\}$ has that profile. Write $F_{w,\theta}$ for its upper-tail area, $N=(E_{1,p}+E_{R,q})/2$ for $R\ge1$, $Q(R,p,q)=|N\cap\{s\ge0\}|$, and $J(\alpha)=Q+F_{1,p}(\alpha)+F_{R,q}(-\alpha)$. The polygon $N$ is the hull of the at most sixteen vertex midpoints. The minimum of $J$ occurs at one of the six support and mode breakpoints of the two terms in $\alpha$, a stationary point of a strictly convex intervening quadratic, or the plateau. Every tested tilt and area is rational for rational profile data.

Write $a'=1-p$, $b'=1-q$, $S=(1+R+a'+Rb')/3$ and $H=(2p-1+R(2q-1))/6$. For $H\le0$,
$$
Q=\begin{cases}
S/2-a'/4+(S-a')^2/(4R^2b'),&a'\le R^2b',\\
S/(2R)-b'/4+(S-Rb')^2/(4a'),&a'\ge R^2b'.
\end{cases}
$$
For $H\ge0$, $Q(R,p,q)=m-Q(R,1-p,1-q)$, with $m=|N|$ equal to $(R+1)/2$ when $p\le R^2q,\ a'\le R^2b'$, to $(1+p/R+Rb')/2$ when $p>R^2q$, and to $(1+Rq+a'/R)/2$ when $a'>R^2b'$. Use the polygon or a continuous limit at zero denominators.
title: Exact midpoint roofs and finite tilt minimization for triangle tents
